question.problem:
Solve for $x$ in $Ax=b$ given that the matrix $A$ is orthogonal, and 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15} & \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3} & \frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Hence, since $A$ is orthogonal, we have ${A}^{-1}={A}^{T}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ {A}^{-1}Ax & ={A}^{-1}b \\ x & ={A}^{-1}b \\ x & ={A}^{T}b \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{15} \\ \frac{2}{3} & 0 & \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{4\sqrt{5}}{15}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
